quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000 (§21.1); "Fees" (§1.5) is a substantive base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. §21.3 places outside the cap breaches of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap. §21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or hidden liability limitation appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.

verification.notes: The inserted Section 10.3 supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: 6-month transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format measured from expiry or termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter. The "at Customer's request" condition attaches only to limb (a) transition assistance, which is inherently elective; the mandatory data-return, deletion, and certification obligations in limbs (b) and (c) are not gated by any request, so the request condition does not swallow post-termination data return. Minimality holds: the document previously had no exit/data-return mechanic (Section 10.1 merely preserved existing rights and 16.5 deferred Customer Data to other sections), so a single concise new subsection is the least intrusive fix; no existing sentence was rewritten or deleted. Intent is preserved: refund, Deliverable-delivery, and confidentiality provisions remain untouched, no defined term is created, and "Customer Data" and "Order Form" are used as defined. Noted in rationale only (not a deviation): the softener "reasonable" before "transition assistance" and the absence of a fix to Section 16.5's cross-reference to a non-existent Section 11 leave minor imprecision, but neither defeats a preferred element.
